note: Story formats: HOW an episode tells its story (the pillar is WHAT it is about). Every week each format is scored like the pillars (7-day views on YouTube + Instagram + Facebook vs the channel median); winners get most new episodes, ~30% keep testing the rest. Add your own: id, name, recipe.

formats.name: The mystery
formats.recipe: Open on a strange real image and an unanswered question. Each scene adds a clue; the reveal lands in the second half (the music peak). The loop line re-opens the mystery.

formats.name: How big is it really
formats.recipe: One number that is hard to imagine, made physical: compare it step by step with things the viewer knows (a city, a country, a lifetime). Use 'stat' overlays for each step and a 'compare' overlay when there are two sizes.

formats.name: Countdown
formats.recipe: A ranked list of 3 (Short) or 5 (long video) real examples, counting down to the most surprising one. Kicker label = the rank ('No. 3'). Never invent a ranking: rank by a number from the source.

formats.name: Then vs now
formats.recipe: The same place or thing at two moments in time. Alternate THEN and NOW scenes; label them in the kicker sub; end on what changed and why.

formats.name: What happens if
formats.recipe: A 'what would happen if...' question answered only with what really happened or what the source says. Build the chain of consequences scene by scene, the biggest consequence last.

formats.name: Myth vs fact
formats.recipe: Start with what most people believe ('You've probably heard that...'), then show with real footage and the source why the truth is different and more interesting.

formats.name: How it happened
formats.recipe: A true event told in order as a mini-thriller: a 'chapter' overlay per stage, a date in each kicker sub, the turning point as the music peak.

formats.name: The record holder
formats.recipe: The fastest, deepest, biggest, oldest: one record, why it is so extreme, and what it took. A 'stat' overlay for the record number, a 'compare' overlay against the runner-up or an everyday thing.
